channel.title: Security Brief
channel.description: Original analysis and ranked cybersecurity news with links to original sources

item.title: The edge is where attackers get in: this week's firewall, VPN and remote-access exploits
item.description: Five exploited flaws in firewalls, VPNs, remote-support software and file-sharing servers show one pattern. The systems that sit at the edge of your network, and that administrators manage remotely, are the weakest link. Here is what to check first.

item.title: October 2026 Patch Tuesday: what the Microsoft feed shows and what to do
item.description: The Microsoft feed lists few entries, and most of them are updates to October's release rather than new fixes. The one item that needs planning is a .NET remote code execution flaw that Microsoft has not fixed yet. Identity Web and WSL need version checks if you use them.

item.title: Weekly M365 & Entra Briefing: 13 to 19 October 2026
item.description: Exchange sign-in problems after October Windows Server updates, an identity-based incident at ConnectWise that affected Microsoft 365 tenants, and why device-code abuse is still worth a Conditional Access check.

item.description: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) on Monday confirmed active exploitation of the recently patched PHP2Shell flaws by adding them to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog. The PHP vulnerabilities, both rated 9.2 on the CVSS scoring system, facilitate unauthenticated remote…

item.description: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) on Friday added two vulnerabilities impacting Collabora Online Built-in CODE Server and Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator (VCO) to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV), citing reports of active exploitation in the wild. The critical-severity…

item.title: Arista Warns of Critical VeloCloud SQL Injection Zero-Day Exploited in Attacks
item.description: Attackers are exploiting a zero-day SQL injection flaw in Arista's VeloCloud Orchestrator (VCO), the central management system for VeloCloud SD-WAN networks, the company said in an advisory on October 22. The flaw lets anyone who can log in to the orchestrator, even with a read-only customer account, gain operator…

item.title: New Cisco firewall zero-day exploited to crash SSL VPN devices
item.description: Cisco released security updates to patch a denial-of-service zero-day in Adaptive Security Appliance (ASA) and Threat Defense (FTD) software that attackers are exploiting to remotely crash vulnerable firewall devices.

item.title: Chinese Hackers Quietly Used Low-Severity ESXi Logging Flaw as Zero-Day
item.description: CVE-2026-41709 allows attackers with administrative privileges to perform operations without being logged. The post Chinese Hackers Quietly Used Low-Severity ESXi Logging Flaw as Zero-Day appeared first on SecurityWeek.

item.title: ShinyHunters-Exploited Oracle PeopleSoft Zero-Day Turns Out to Be Three Chained Flaws
item.description: The critical Oracle PeopleSoft bug that ShinyHunters has exploited since May is not one flaw but three chained together, the researchers who reported it said this week. Oracle patched all three under a single identifier, CVE-2026-35273, in June. Its root is a server-side request forgery (SSRF) that reaches an internal…

item.title: Apple Backports Fix for Exploited CoreGraphics Flaw to Older iPhones and iPads
item.description: Apple on Monday backported fixes for a high-severity security flaw that was exploited in real-world cyber attacks to older devices. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-86950 (CVSS score: 8.8), is an out-of-bounds write affecting CoreGraphics that could result in arbitrary code execution when processing a…

item.title: Even after PHP2Shell, blast radius matters more than a CVSS score
item.description: PHP2Shell shows how quickly attackers can exploit critical vulnerabilities, often before organizations have time to patch. Token Security explains why limiting the access of service accounts, API keys, and AI agents is just as important as fixing vulnerabilities to reduce the damage from a breach.

item.title: Japan's GMO urges customers to shut down PCs amid ransomware threat
item.description: The GMO Group has urged customers to disconnect their systems from the internet and shut down computers after a threat actor who breached the company's Onamae Desktop Cloud threatened to launch a ransomware attack today.

item.description: CWE added. Informational change only.

item.title: Windows 11 KB5127936 update released with 41 changes and fixes
item.description: Microsoft released the KB5127936 preview cumulative update for Windows 11 versions 25H2 and 26H2, with 41 changes, including File Explorer and Cloud rebuild improvements.

item.description: Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of what appears to be an artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted attack orchestrated by a suspected China-nexus threat actor that has leveraged the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities to breach exposed systems. The activity, which was observed on October 25, 2026, involved an…

item.title: CVE-2026-62877 Windows Win32k Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability
item.description: Added supported editions of Microsoft Office to the Security Updates table because they are affected by this vulnerability. Microsoft recommends that customers running any of these editions of Office install the latest security updates to be fully protected from this vulnerability.

item.title: Exposed Infrastructure Reveals How Ransomware Affiliates Used AI Agents to Execute Intrusions
item.description: Cybersecurity researchers have discovered an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven intrusion ecosystem run by affiliates of the INC and The Gentlemen ransomware groups. Central to the operation is an "Autonomous Red Team Kill Chain Framework" referred to as Phantom. The threat actor is assessed to be Russian-speaking…

item.title: Microsoft fixes Remote Desktop failures caused by recent Windows updates
item.description: Microsoft has resolved a known issue that prevents non-admin users from connecting to devices via Remote Desktop when the "Administrator protection" security feature is enabled.

item.title: Adobe, Veeam, Juniper Networks Patch Critical Vulnerabilities
item.description: The flaws could lead to arbitrary code execution, authorization bypasses, and privilege escalation. The post Adobe, Veeam, Juniper Networks Patch Critical Vulnerabilities appeared first on SecurityWeek.

item.title: BAE Says No Data Extracted in Incident Hitting Bankruptcy Courts
item.description: BAE Systems says no data was extracted and no PII was breached in the incident that disrupted US bankruptcy court notices for weeks. The post BAE Says No Data Extracted in Incident Hitting Bankruptcy Courts appeared first on SecurityWeek.

item.title: 26,400 Valid Cloud and AI Credentials Found Exposed in Public Gitee Repositories
item.description: 26,400 credentials that developers left in public code on Gitee, a Chinese code-hosting service, still worked when a researcher tested them. Anyone who copied one from that code could have used it. Independent researcher Ben Zimmermann found them by scanning 7.25 million public Gitee repositories and reported the…

item.title: Attacker Tried to Exploit Alpine Linux’s GitLab via CVSS 10.0 Flaw Its Ruby Left Open
item.description: An attacker tried to exploit a critical GitLab vulnerability on the Alpine Linux project's own GitLab server a week after GitLab released a fix, Alpine Linux said on 28 October. The flaw, CVE-2026-97229 (CVSS score: 10.0), can let an attacker run code on a GitLab server through a crafted regular expression in a CI…

item.title: HHS Filing Puts iRhythm Data Breach Toll at 8.2 Million
item.description: Hackers stole personal information and iRhythm account and device data from third-party-hosted business applications. The post HHS Filing Puts iRhythm Data Breach Toll at 8.2 Million appeared first on SecurityWeek.

item.title: Hackers Exploited Cisco SD-WAN Flaw to Plant Malware Built to Steal Encryption Keys
item.description: Hackers exploited a critical Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN flaw, fixed in February, to plant custom malware inside the systems that control an organization's SD-WAN network. The malware, called KeyDrift, is designed to copy the keys that encrypt traffic between sites and store them for later use, Cisco Talos said on October…

item.title: Japan Airlines warns of data breach as country grapples with multiple cyber incidents
item.description: Hackers stole passport numbers, frequent flyer numbers, email addresses and phone numbers for about 2,000 customers.

item.title: Sony ISP subsidiary data breach exposes 2.5 million customer records
item.description: Sony Network Communications has confirmed a data breach that compromised approximately 2.5 million records containing current and former customers' personal information.

item.title: Researcher Reveals How Logic Bugs Alone Cracked Microsoft Edge in $175,000 Pwn2Own Win
item.description: A chain of logic flaws, with no memory corruption, can turn a malicious web page into code running on a Windows computer outside Microsoft Edge's sandbox, a security researcher has shown. Orange Tsai of DEVCORE published the full method on October 28, five months after the chain won $175,000 at the Pwn2Own Berlin…

item.title: UK to look at making software companies liable for cyber breaches
item.description: The new U.K. budget says the government will "consider where liability for cyber breaches should sit," potentially a landmark shift for a country that has relied on voluntary codes to encourage software vendors to improve security.

item.title: Ukrainian Hive and Nefilim Ransomware Affiliate Gets 70 Months in US Prison
item.description: Artem Stryzhak was sentenced to 70 months in prison after pleading guilty to using Nefilim ransomware in attacks. The post Ukrainian Hive and Nefilim Ransomware Affiliate Gets 70 Months in US Prison appeared first on SecurityWeek.

The vulnerability in question is CVE-2026-101767 (CVSS score: 9.8), a case of improper authentication in the Oracle Application Object Library of Oracle…

item.title: Anthropic's Unreleased AI Model Chains Flaws Into Working Chrome, Safari, Windows and Linux Exploits
item.description: An unreleased Anthropic AI model found security flaws in Chrome, Safari, Android, Windows, and Linux and chained them into working proof-of-concept exploits, the company said in its latest report. The exploits were built in the lab after the model was prompted, not seen in any real attack, and Anthropic reported every…

item.title: Japan's GMO Offers $1 Million Bounty to Catch Hackers Behind FX Trading Cloud Breach
item.description: Japan's GMO Internet Group is offering up to $1 million in total for tips that help catch the attackers who breached its Onamae.com Desktop Cloud service, after refusing to pay an extortion demand. The reward program opened on October 28 and pays only if a tip helps lead to an arrest or an international wanted notice…

item.title: Warp discloses breach exposing AI agent logs, user telemetry data
item.description: Agent decision logs and telemetry data belonging to Warp agentic development environment users were exposed in an attack on a third-party vendor in the project's infrastructure.

item.title: CISA warns of PHP bug exploitation attempts, gives federal agencies days to patch
item.description: CISA added the widely publicized PHP vulnerabilities to the KEV, but didn't specify what kind of exploitation it was observing.

item.title: CISA confirms PHP2Shell vulnerabilities now exploited in attacks
item.description: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has added the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities to its catalog of actively exploited security flaws and ordered federal agencies to patch their systems by Thursday.

item.title: Attackers Use Microsoft Teams IT Support Scams to Deploy Malware and Ransomware
item.description: Cybersecurity researchers are calling attention to what they say is a "recurring social engineering pattern" across hundreds of cases in which threat actors use Microsoft Teams' external chat creation feature to conduct impersonation scams or to deliver malware. item.title: Microsoft releases emergency .NET patches for critical Brotli flaw
item.description: Microsoft released emergency.NET security updates to patch a critical vulnerability known as Broccoli2Shell, also tracked as Node2Shell and HTTP2Shell.

item.title: Reports of PHP bug exploitation attempts grow as experts downplay viability of exploits
